messages:
alex: Ran an nsys capture on the nightly inference job. Seeing CPU enqueue gaps (~100ms) between kernel launches and a long `cudaMemcpyAsync` on stream 2 that overlaps the kernels on stream 1 — but kernels appear stalled. Posting the minimal nsys snippet and command I used.

Command:```nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o nightly_run nsys_target -- ./bin/serve --profile=short```

nsys timeline excerpt (timestamps are relative ms):
[0.0] host: enqueue kernel A -> stream 1
[1.2] host: enqueue kernel B -> stream 1
[1.3] host: enqueue memcpy 20.0MB -> stream 2 (`cudaMemcpyAsync`)
[1.4] stream 2: memcpy start (20.0MB)
[1.4] stream 1: kernel A start
[1.6] stream 1: kernel A end
[1.6] stream 1: kernel B start (but stalled)
[19.8] stream 2: memcpy end
[19.9] stream 1: kernel B actually runs

Observation: kernel B shows device-side 'ready' but doesn't execute until the memcpy finishes, which implies copy engine activity is somehow blocking scheduling/SM progress or launch ordering is getting serialized on the host side.

---

tori: can you attach the full .qdrep? also is the memcpy pinned-host or pageable? if it's pageable the driver will issue a synchronous host->device staging which can stall. :eyes:

alex: I don't have the qdrep here (CI deletes after 24h). Quick check: buffers are created with normal malloc (so pageable). Code path is the KV prefetcher doing `cudaMemcpyAsync(host_buf, device_buf, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream)` without explicit `cudaHostAlloc`/pinned.

deepa: that matches. Pageable->GPU async copy does a host-side staging which blocks the host thread while the copy engine runs, and nsys will show host CPU busy during that window. But your snippet shows an actual host enqueue gap before the memcpy completes — that could be the host thread blocked on the staging. Are we using our worker pinned pool?

perf-bot: perf alert: nightly_inference latency P50 +12% vs baseline (2026-03-15). Traces attached to CI run 17949.

alex: good call. I'm pretty sure the KV prefetch runs on the same host thread that enqueues kernels; we do prefetch then enqueue next kernel expecting overlap. If prefetch uses pageable memory, the staging will block the enqueue loop.

kevin: two quick checks: 1) ensure prefetch uses pinned host memory (cudaHostAlloc or cudaHostRegister), 2) avoid `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` in that path, 3) check for `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING` env var on CI. Also run `nvml` counters for PCIe utilization during the memcpy to see if bandwidth is normal.

deepa: also check that the memcpy isn't implicitly using the default stream semantics (i.e., a blocking copy to the default stream can serialize). If user code passes `0` stream or mixes default stream semantics, you can get ordering surprises.

alex: quick micro numbers from the run: memcpy sizes [8MB, 20MB, 12MB] -> durations [7.1ms, 18.9ms, 10.8ms]. PCIe bandwidth implied is ~1.05-1.1 GB/s which is much lower than expected (should be ~12-16 GB/s for PCIe gen3 x16). So something is off (staging + CPU bottleneck).

tori: wow 1.1 GB/s is too low. Could be pinned vs pageable causing extra memcpy to staging buffer in host memory. Also check numa bindings and whether the buffer is on a remote NUMA node causing cross-socket copy slowdown. `numactl --show` on the worker process and `nvidia-smi topo -m` would help.

kevin: agree. Another hypothesis: our prefetch thread set has a low scheduling priority and the OS preempted it while the copy engine was busy; if the host thread is blocked doing a synchronous staging copy the scheduler can delay it, creating the long tail. Use `perf sched` or capture `sched_switch` in perfetto/nsys (osrt) to confirm.

alex: next steps I will run two repros: 1) switch prefetch to cudaHostAlloc mapped pinned buffers and re-run nsys; 2) run the same workload but force the prefetch to a dedicated pinned-thread (pthread pinned to CPU core) and capture `--trace=osrt` to see any sched switches. I'll post results.

deepa: if pinned buffers fix it that's a simple patch. If not, also try moving prefetch to its own CUDA stream and ensure we launch kernels from a different host thread so enqueue ordering can't block.

tori: add a micro-benchmark: `cudaMemcpyAsync` from pinned vs pageable and measure host-side blocking. Also try `cudaMemcpy` vs `cudaMemcpyAsync` to see behavior.

alex: ack. I'll run quick tests and update in this thread. Thanks for the triage. :thumbsup:

kevin: FWIW, check our Triton/runner layer too — sometimes we do unexpected `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` for error-checking on the release build. Grep for `cudaDeviceSynchronize` in the prefetch & enqueue path.

alex: noted, will grep. If anyone wants to follow the capture I'll upload the qdrep to the perf bucket once I have the pinned-buffer run.

---
